alignments.note: Infinitive expanded into a finite clause: the supplied complementizer belongs to it (rule 85), and the supplied *how* completing *know how* rides with it, discontinuously under rule 15.
Distributive adjective with the supplied generic *one*; head on the adjective (rule 17).
Partitive genitive rendered *of you*, headed on the pronoun.
Article displaced by the possessive *his own*, which the reflexive ἑαυτοῦ carries (rule 20).

Middle infinitive rendered by the phrasal *possess himself of*; the reflexive object and the phrasal *of* are the verb's own, the Greek object being accusative and so realized by no case preposition (rule 106).
Reflexive genitive rendered by the possessive *his own* (rule 20).
Head noun standing bare behind the possessive.
Preposition realized by its own word.

review_notes: *that* and *how* both ride with εἰδέναι under rule 85, the infinitive being the clause the ASV expands.

The reflexive *himself* of *possess himself of* is the middle verb's own English, distinct from the possessive *his own* that renders ἑαυτοῦ; reading *himself* as the reflexive's realization instead remains defensible.
